newsitem.title: USA: Business inventories rose in August.
newsitem.headline: Business inventories rose in August.

text.p: Stocks of unsold goods on the shelves of wholesalers, retailers and manufacturers rose in August to the highest level on record, the Commerce Department said Thursday.

Total business inventories rose 0.5 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted $1 trillion, which was the highest level on record since the department began tracking the data in 1982, a spokeswoman said.
The August increase in total stocks of unsold goods was higher than the 0.3 percent increase forecast by Wall Street economists.
July inventories were revised upward to a 0.5 percent increase from the previously reported 0.4 percent rise.
Retail inventories rose 0.7 percent to $311.11 billion, after a 1.5 percent rise in July.
Auto inventories, which show up in the retail figures, rose by 1.5 percent to $87.8 billion in August.
Manufacturers' inventories rose by 0.3 percent to $435.61 billion. That followed a revised 0.1 percent rise in July, which was previously reported as a 0.2 percent increase.
Wholesalers' inventories rose 0.5 percent to $260.31 billion after a 0.1 percent drop in July, which was revised downward from the previously reported 0.1 percent increase.
Total business sales in August fell by 0.3 percent to $717.09 billion, after a revised 1 percent increase in July that was previously reported as a 1.2 percent increase.
The inventory-to-sales ratio, a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace, rose to 1.40 months' worth in August from 1.39 months in July.
